xy: (genetics) normal complement of sex hormones in a male
xylaria: type genus of Xylariaceae; fungi with perithecia in the upper part of erect black woody stromata
xylaria mali: fungus causing black root rot in apples
xylaria polymorpha: the fruiting bodies of the fungi of the genus Xylaria
xylariaceae: family of fungi characterized by dark brown to black spores
xylem: the woody part of plants: the supporting and water-conducting tissue, consisting primarily of tracheids and vessels
xylene: a colorless flammable volatile liquid hydrocarbon used as a solvent
xylocaine: a local anesthetic (trade names Lidocaine and Xylocaine) used topically on the skin and mucous membranes
xylol: a colorless flammable volatile liquid hydrocarbon used as a solvent
xylomelum: small species of Australian trees or shrubs; grown for their fruit and flowers
xylomelum pyriforme: tree bearing pear-shaped fruit with a thick woody epicarp
xylophone: a percussion instrument with wooden bars tuned to produce a chromatic scale and with resonators; played with small mallets
xylopia: tropical evergreen trees or shrubs; chiefly African
xylopia aethiopica: tropical west African evergreen tree bearing pungent aromatic seeds used as a condiment and in folk medicine
xylose: a sugar extracted from wood or straw; used in foods for diabetics
xylosma: shrub or small tree grown as an ornamental in mild climates for its neat evergreen foliage and fragrant late flowers; native of China
xylosma congestum: shrub or small tree grown as an ornamental in mild climates for its neat evergreen foliage and fragrant late flowers; native of China
xyphophorus helleri: freshwater fish of Central America having a long swordlike tail; popular aquarium fish
xyridaceae: plants of tropical to temperate regions; usually in wet places
xyris: chiefly American marsh plants, having usually yellow flowers
xyy: (genetics) abnormal complement of sex hormones in a male who has two Y chromosomes
